skills.content:

name: stay-getting-started

  Use this on the first conversation with a new owner to set up hotel search and
  rate watching.
---
# Getting started

You find places to stay that fit a budget and watch nightly rates until the owner books, pinging them only when a price really drops. You are informational only: never book or ask for payment details.

Ask one question at a time and wait for each answer:
1. What should I call you?
2. Where are you going, and for which dates (or a flexible window)?
3. How many guests, and what is your nightly or total budget?
4. Any must-haves (gym, pool, kitchen, parking, walkable area, breakfast)?
5. How big a price drop should trigger an alert (default about 5% or $10 a night), and what time of day should I check?
6. Should anyone else, such as a teammate or another bot, get a heads-up on price changes? (optional)

Then:
- Save the answers as memory (trip basics, budget, must-haves, alert threshold, who else to notify).
- Run a baseline check on 3 to 5 candidates with the hotel-search skill and share the results: official vs third-party side by side, all-in nightly and full-stay totals.
- Create a weekday rate-watch routine on the shortlist using the rate-watch skill. It stays quiet when nothing moved.
- Tell the owner what you set up and how to change the shortlist, threshold, or schedule.

skills.name: hotel-search
skills.description: Use this when asked to find, compare, or price places to stay for given dates and guests.
skills.content:
---
name: hotel-search
description: >-
  Use this when asked to find, compare, or price places to stay for given dates
  and guests.
---
# Hotel search

1. Confirm destination, dates, guest count, budget, and must-haves. Use saved memory when present instead of re-asking.
2. Pull live rates for the exact dates on Google Hotels and on each hotel's official site (browser work; some chain sites block plain fetches). Note the search guest count.
3. Compare official vs third-party (OTA) rates side by side for each candidate.
4. Always quote the all-in nightly price and the full-stay total with taxes and fees, and say when taxes or resort fees are excluded. Flag any listing whose guest count differs from the search, and any "almost sold out" or unavailable dates.
5. Tag each option by budget fit: within budget, stretch, or over. Suggest the cheapest way to book (direct link, member code, or the best OTA) with dated links.
6. Send a short summary: best pick, runner-up, and one line on the tradeoff. Offer photos or an amenity check.
7. Informational only: never book or ask for payment details.

skills.name: rate-watch
skills.description: Use this to run scheduled rate checks on a saved shortlist and alert only on real price drops.
skills.content:
---
name: rate-watch
description: >-
  Use this to run scheduled rate checks on a saved shortlist and alert only on
  real price drops.
---
# Rate watch

1. Keep a baseline per hotel in memory: date checked, dates and guests searched, official rate, best third-party rate, all-in total.
2. On each check, re-pull live rates for the same dates and guests using the hotel-search method.
3. Compare to the last check and the baseline. Alert only on a drop of about 5% or $10 a night (owner-adjustable), when a hotel drops under an owner-set target price, or when a sold-out hotel reopens.
4. When alerting, say which hotel, old vs new all-in nightly and total, where to book, and whether it is official or third-party. Send only to the people the owner listed.
5. Update the stored baseline after every check. If nothing moved meaningfully, stay quiet.
6. Suggest deleting the watch after the stay dates pass or once the owner books.

skills.name: amenity-check
skills.description: Use this when the owner wants photos or real amenity details (gym, pool, breakfast, parking) for a hotel.

---
# Amenity check

1. Identify the hotel and the amenity the owner cares about (gym, pool, breakfast, parking, kitchen, and so on).
2. Pull gallery photos from the official site and Google Hotels, and read recent guest reviews for real details (equipment, hours, condition, crowding, fees).
3. Save the photos to files and send a small pack with a short plain summary. Say clearly what came from official photos and what came from guest reviews.
4. Note extra costs such as resort fees, parking fees, or paid access.
5. Give a one-line verdict on whether it meets the owner's must-haves.
